names.note: The calendar’s own name page for him, which day-candidates.mjs prints as `name: Иларион (Троицкий), архиепископ Верейский`; the rank is stripped and the surname kept, the day line itself declining the forename and the see only. `fk.mjs` on the stored string returns NONE, against twenty-five Hilarion folders and twelve folders whose name carries «Троицкий».

birth.note: Both readings the calendar links give the day as well as the year: «родился 13 сентября 1886 года в семье священника с. Липицы Каширского уезда». They disagree on the province — the first says Тульской, the second Московской — and the disagreement is recorded in the life rather than resolved.

death.note: The day line closes «(1929)» and both readings date the death «15/28 декабря 1929 года», the Julian day of this memory with its civil equivalent beside it. The second reading adds the cause, typhus caught on the transport, and the place, a prison hospital in Leningrad.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 15 декабря ст. ст. — «Сщмч. Илариона, архиеп. Верейского (1929).»

attestations.note: The day’s fifth entry. Two readings stand behind it at `/Life/id9113.htm`, an index, and both were opened: `/Life/life6602.htm` and `/Life/life4812.htm`. No folder held him — `fk.mjs` on «Иларион (Троицкий)» returns NONE, and a Cyrillic grep for «Троицкий» over every `saint.json` returns twelve folders, none of them this man. The office is `Archbishop`, the word both readings and the name page use; the see is in the display name and in the life, because `Archbishop of Vereya` is not a string the four locale packs read. `new-martyr` is written as this corpus writes it for this calendar’s twentieth-century «сщмч.» entries, AND THE 26 ЯНВАРЯ SYNAXIS PAGE WAS NOT OPENED. HIS «ДНИ ПАМЯТИ» LINE PRINTS SIX DAYS — «26 января (Новомуч.), 27 апреля (прославление), 8 июня (Петерб.), 11 июля (обретение мощей), 24 августа (Моск.), 15 декабря» — and only the last of them is the day page that listed him, so only the last is this row; the others are a glorification, a finding of relics and two diocesan synaxes, and none of them is recorded as a feast. The day page carries eight hymn blocks and not one of them is under his name.
